journeys.negative_control: AAASM-6272's bug cluster (AAASM-6280/6281/6282) pinned each fix against the pre-fix behavior before it was corrected -- see each test's own doc comment for the adversarial/positive-control pair. AAASM-6272 (D1/D2/D4) proved the attenuation-ceiling refusal logic correct through `resolve_boundary`-shaped fixtures with `Ancestry::Parent` constructed directly in the test harness -- real in-process gating, not a live cross-process handoff. The remaining gap is cross-process parent-authority handoff (a real supervisor process attesting a real child process's resolved `ParentAuthority`), which AAASM-6273 owns as its own Story -- still `partial`, not `automated`, until that handoff exists. AAASM-6290 (ST-3, independent QA) re-ran `cargo nextest run -p aa-isolation --lib attenuation:: authority::` (32/32 pass) and `cargo nextest run -p aa-cli --test run_command --test run_exec_target` (17/17 pass), and added a real 3-generation (root -> child -> grandchild) attenuation-chain test built end to end through `DelegationLedger::derive_child`: widening at generation 2 (a sibling scope of the child's own grant, still inside the root's) is correctly refused as `ChildExceedsParent` against the immediate parent specifically, with a positive control proving the identical lease admits when checked directly against the root instead. Found one real gap in the revocation leg, documented rather than fixed (QA scope, verified by direct probe, not assumed): revoking the root's lease is caught for the hop re-gated directly against it (the immediate child is refused via `LeaseInvalid::Revoked`, and the ledger refuses to mint any fresh child from the revoked lease) -- but an already-minted, already-held grandchild `ParentAuthority` whose own immediate parent (the child lease) was never itself revoked is NOT retroactively invalidated: the grandchild still gates cleanly against that held ancestry, and a fresh grandchild can still be minted from the still-active child lease through the same ledger. `RevocationState` lives per lease object (its own doc comment already says propagation latency is unmeasured and unclaimed) and `check_attenuation` only ever inspects the immediate parent, never the whole ancestry chain, so "revocation cascades to reach the grandchild" does not hold for an already-resolved deeper snapshot. The target contract is pinned as an `#[ignore]`d failing test (`a_grandchild_is_refused_once_any_ancestor_up_to_the_root_is_revoked_target_contract`); candidate Bug not yet filed. ST-3 also checked `aa-cli`'s `--root-agent` refusal message wording in `run_command.rs`/`run_exec_target.rs`: both correctly name AAASM-6273 as the tracking ticket for cross-process ancestry resolution and accurately describe why the launch is refused rather than silently treated as rootless -- no documentation-accuracy finding there. `lifecycle_state` stays `partial`. AAASM-6307 then fixed that transitive-revocation gap in `aa-isolation` (the ledger records parent edges, `derive_child` refuses under any revoked ancestor, and `ParentAuthority` carries the live ledger so `authority_gate` walks the whole chain and fails closed on an unknown one); the former `#[ignore]`d target test now runs and passes, and the characterization test asserts refusal. That fix is awaiting independent review and has not been independently verified, so it is not counted as closed here; the cross-process handoff AAASM-6273 owns also remains open.

journeys.negative_control: AAASM-6272 (AAASM-6278/6277) proved the policy-authored egress contract reaches every isolation intent and that a `broker_required` policy under `--isolation none` now refuses instead of silently launching unconfined (closing the fail-open gap #2616 fixed), plus cloud-metadata-service default-deny. AAASM-6261's own acceptance contract also requires identity attribution verifiable in audit/evidence output (today only `EgressAuthority::identity`, documented as asserted-not-verified) and that a policy change narrowing egress takes effect on the next connection attempt (every gate test here runs once, at launch -- no dynamic re-evaluation is exercised). Those two remain a genuine gap, not yet `automated`. AAASM-6292 (ST-5, independent QA) additionally live-verified the full `--isolation {none,process,auto}` x `broker_required` refusal matrix on a real macOS host (all three fail closed, each for a correctly-ordered reason -- `none` at the egress-contract check itself, `process`/`auto` earlier at backend-selection since no Linux/`aasm-macos-vm` backend is configured here -- never a silent admit) and found one real classifier gap: `classify_destination` (and `aa_core::net::blocked_ip_literal`, which `aa-proxy`'s own CONNECT literal check shares) parses a host via `std::str::FromStr<IpAddr>`, which does not accept decimal/octal/hex numeric IPv4 notation (`2852039166` for `169.254.169.254`), so that encoding is classified as a `Name` needing only a NameResolution grant rather than as a `RestrictedAddress` the per-destination check would refuse -- documented as an `#[ignore]`d failing test rather than fixed there. AAASM-6304 then fixed it at the host-classification layer: `aa_core::net::parse_ip_literal` (inet_aton rules: decimal/hex/octal/1-4 part IPv4, plus std IPv4/IPv6) now backs both `classify_destination` and `blocked_ip_literal`, the test is un-ignored, and unit tests cover decimal, hex, octal, short-form and mixed spellings plus a public-address control and name negatives; an independent review differentially tested the first fix against the macOS libc and found it regressed leading-zero dotted forms (inet_aton reads them as octal, getaddrinfo as decimal), so the parser was rewritten to fail closed: it evaluates every plausible resolver reading and reports a restricted address if any reading is restricted, and refuses (0.0.0.0 sentinel) a literal whose public readings disagree or that only resolves public via 32-bit truncation. Four independent reviews differentially tested the parser against the libc of the macOS host it ran on and each found a new gap, all fixed: leading-zero dotted forms; a lone value of 2^32 or more, and then a part of 2^64 or more inside a multi-part literal (e.g. 169.254.169.18446744073709551870 is 169.254.169.254 because macOS accumulates each part modulo 2^64, while 169.254.169.4294967550 is rejected); an empty IPv6 zone id; strings no libc accepts reported routable (`08.1`, `1.0x`, `8.8.8.8.`, a lone invalid-octal value like `0123456789`); IPv6 spellings `std` rejects but getaddrinfo accepts (`::ffff:169.254.169.0254`, `::ffff:0a9fe:a9fe`, `0fe80::1`), now refused structurally (any colon-bearing string of only hex digits, colons and dots that `std` does not accept is refused, `host:port` pairs excepted); and a zone id containing whitespace. A permitted-literal egress exception matches only the canonical spelling. After the fixes, across about 1.9 million literals in several corpora (the fourth review added IPv6 transition prefixes, `host:port` shapes, Unicode and control characters, very long strings, hex-letter hostnames and mutation fuzz) no restricted `inet_aton`/`inet_addr`/`getaddrinfo` reading is left unrefused; `inet_network` readings are not a connect path and are not counted. The remaining differences are strings with trailing text after whitespace whose head is public (`8.8.8.8 x`), which stay names; an interior NUL (which C truncates but Rust `CString` and `ToSocketAddrs` reject); and policy outside this ticket (Teredo, SIIT, `fec0::/10` and multicast are treated as routable). Local mutations of each rule, including the multi-part wrap, the port-pair exemption and the structural IPv6 refusal, each turn at least one suite red; full `--lib` runs are aa-core 571, aa-isolation 256 and aa-proxy 358 (3 skipped) passing. The mutation and differential runs are local, not in CI, and the libc readings come from one macOS host (glibc rejects the wrapped literals). A resolver or libc neither the corpora nor the table model could still disagree, and a final review of the last head is pending; this row stays partial. See AAASM-6284's verification comment for the full AC-by-AC mapping.
